subject: mathematics
question_text: In a △ABC, if a : b : c = 7 : 8 : 9, then show that cos A : cos B : cos C = 14 : 11 : 6.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Introduce the constant k
steps.margin_note: No separate mark at this length. A ratio fixes the sides only up to a scale, so write a = 7k, b = 8k, c = 9k. The k will cancel out of every cosine.

recall.must_convey: That the ratio is written with a constant k: a = 7k, b = 8k, c = 9k.
accept: write a as seven k b as eight k and c as nine k
introduce a constant because a ratio does not fix the sizes
take the sides as seven k eight k nine k
a seven k, b eight k, c nine k ani rasta
put in a proportionality constant

steps.why: Ratios give shape, not size. The k carries the size and then cancels — which is why the answer is the same for every triangle with these proportions.
common_mistakes: Taking a = 7, b = 8, c = 9 directly, which is only one case.
Using a different constant for each side.

steps.label: Find cos A
steps.margin_note: One of the two marks, and it covers the cosine-rule work for all three angles. The cosine rule, with the k² cancelling top and bottom. Every cosine below works the same way.

recall.must_convey: That the cosine rule gives cos A = 96/144 = 2/3, with k² cancelling.
accept: use the cosine rule, the k squared cancels and cos A is ninety six over one forty four which is two thirds
cos A comes to two over three
the constant cancels leaving a pure number
k square cancel ayi cos A two by three vasthundi
apply the cosine rule for A

steps.why: k² appears in every term of both numerator and denominator, so it cancels completely. That is what makes the answer independent of the triangle's size.
common_mistakes: Subtracting the wrong side: for cos A it is a² that is subtracted.

steps.label: Find cos B and cos C
steps.margin_note: No separate mark of its own — it is covered by the mark above. Same rule, rotating which side is subtracted: b² for cos B, c² for cos C.

recall.must_convey: That cos B = 11/21 and cos C = 2/7, each from the cosine rule with the matching side subtracted.
accept: cos B is eleven over twenty one and cos C is two over seven
rotate which side is subtracted for each angle
the other two cosines come out as eleven twenty firsts and two sevenths
cos B eleven by twenty one, cos C two by seven
apply the cosine rule for the other two angles

steps.why: The rule always subtracts the side OPPOSITE the angle being found. Keeping that straight is the whole bookkeeping of the step.

steps.label: Form the ratio
steps.margin_note: The last mark. The three fractions have denominators 3, 21 and 7 — all divide 21, so multiplying every term by 21 clears them at once.
lines: cos A : cos B : cos C = 2/3 : 11/21 : 2/7

recall.must_convey: That multiplying all three by 21 (their common denominator) clears the fractions to give 14 : 11 : 6.
accept: multiply all three by twenty one to clear the fractions giving fourteen eleven six
the common denominator is twenty one so multiply through
the ratio is fourteen to eleven to six
twenty one tho multiply cheste fourteen eleven six vasthundi
clear the denominators to get the ratio

steps.why: A ratio is unchanged when every term is multiplied by the same number, so 21 can be chosen freely — and 21 is the one that clears all three denominators at once.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only some of the terms.
